title: A.R.I.A. Canonical Technical Entity
description: Machine-readable validation schema for canonical technical entities used by A.R.I.A. This schema is subordinate to entity_contracts.json for identity and shared interoperability contracts and to entity_types.json for canonical entity-type vocabulary.

entity_type.description: Canonical entity classification. The value MUST exist in Core/Registries/entity_types.json. This schema intentionally does not duplicate the Registry vocabulary as an enum.

canonical_name.description: Preferred human-readable name for the canonical technical entity. The name may change without changing canonical identity.

description.description: Concise definition of the entity itself. Relationships, case observations, and historical experience should not be serialized into this field.

status.description: Lifecycle status of the canonical entity.

validation_state.description: Validation state of the entity. Entity validation does not automatically validate relationships involving the entity.

aliases.description: Known names, abbreviations, manufacturer terminology, historical terminology, or other labels resolving to this canonical entity. Aliases do not create separate canonical entities.

provenance.description: Provenance describing how the canonical entity entered A.R.I.A.'s knowledge system. Semantics are governed by the provenance contract in Core/Schemas/entity_contracts.json.

confidence.description: Confidence in the quality or support for this entity assertion. Confidence is not probability. Semantics are governed by the confidence contract in Core/Schemas/entity_contracts.json.

valid_from.description: Beginning of the period during which this entity definition or applicability is considered valid when temporally bounded.

valid_to.description: End of the entity's known applicability period. Null means no known end.

superseded_by.description: Canonical identifier of the entity that supersedes this entity when applicable.

legacy_identifiers.description: Historical identifiers retained for migration, reconciliation, and auditability. Legacy identifiers are not authoritative canonical identities.

created_by.description: Canonical actor reference or implementation-defined creator reference when available.

updated_by.description: Canonical actor reference or implementation-defined updater reference when available.

metadata.description: Controlled extensibility for entity-type-specific technical metadata. Metadata must not be used to create hidden relationship systems, duplicate canonical entities, store case-specific evidence, or replace authoritative Registry vocabulary.

canonical_entity_identifier.description: Canonical typed identifier governed by Core/Schemas/entity_contracts.json. The most specific established identity prefix should be used. The generic ent prefix is used for canonical technical entities that do not have a dedicated canonical prefix.

alias_type.description: Optional classification such as abbreviation, manufacturer terminology, historical name, field terminology, alternate spelling, or other implementation-defined alias classification.

source_id.description: Optional canonical source reference supporting this alias.

manufacturer_entity_id.description: Optional manufacturer context when an alias is manufacturer-specific.
